nodes.name: Payload Valid?

nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Order Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Merge Routed Work
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per order (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Order Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. # Alert stakeholders on changes: Google Sheets & Gmail

**Pattern:** Event Notification · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers fulfillment work end to end across Google Sheets, Gmail and Slack.

It moves through 16 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Stamp & Shape Order
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Route by Work Type
6. Process 'standard' → Google Sheets
7. Fast-Track 'priority' + Alert
8. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
9. Merge Routed Work
10. Fingerprint for Idempotency
11. Drop Already-Processed Items
12. Load Previous Snapshot
13. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
14. Summarize Run Stats
15. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
16. Send Summary to Gmail

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing fulfillment work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Stamp & Shape Order → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Route by Work Type → Process 'standard' → Google Sheets → Fast-Track 'priority' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Gmail → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Gmail aligned by hand for fulfillment
- Pushing fulfillment events into Google Sheets and Gmail the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Fulfillment work where "Stamp & Shape Order" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Fulfillment work that only reaches Google Sheets when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Gmail in step for fulfillment, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Gmail are skipped, across all 19 nodes of this fulfillment build
- A failed Google Sheets or Gmail call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this fulfillment build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a fulfillment run reports once rather than 19 times
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for fulfillment

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
fulfillment payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your fulfillment process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
